question.text: The elevation in boiling point for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> molal solution of non-volatile solute <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. The depression in freezing point for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> molal solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> in the same solvent is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. The ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></msub></math> i.e., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> is

solution.text:
We know that

ΔTb=iKbm1ΔTf=iKfm2

And for non-volatile solute i=1.

ΔTbΔTf=Kb×1 Kf×2⇒36=12=KbKf×12

KbKf=11⇒X=1
